heading: How do I reduce a JPG for an upload or email?
introduction: Reduce a JPG or JPEG photo with Balanced, High quality or Maximum while preserving original display dimensions. Use the separate Target size mode when an upload form requires a maximum number of bytes.

sections.heading: Keep a copy of your original JPG
sections.body: Add the photograph and review the default Maximum mode. Choose Balanced for a more moderate trade-off. Compare faces, textures and text at the same scale. High quality retains more detail at a potentially larger size; Maximum prioritizes smaller output with a greater risk of visible artifacts.

sections.heading: A target size is a limit, not an exact byte count
sections.body: Target size searches actual encodes and verifies the final byte count. A 50 KB maximum means 50,000 bytes, not a promise of exactly that size. If no supported encode fits, the result is marked Target not met. Image dimensions stay unchanged.

sections.heading: Where JPG works well
sections.body: JPG suits photographs and many opaque web images. It cannot preserve transparency. Inspect faces, fine textures and lettering, and keep the camera or design original because repeated lossy encoding can add artifacts.

seoTitle: JPG Compressor — Reduce Photo File Size
seoDescription: Compress JPG and JPEG photos with original dimensions by default. Choose quality modes or a verified maximum-byte target, then inspect the real result.
